figures.caption: Trace the two renal origins: ureteric bud to collecting system; metanephric mesenchyme to nephron epithelium. Their interaction is reciprocal. figures.title: An action potential and changing conductance
figures.alt: Aligned graphs show a neuronal action potential, an early increase in relative sodium conductance and a later, longer potassium conductance increase.
figures.caption: Read the two panels together: rapid sodium-channel activation accompanies the upstroke; sodium inactivation and delayed potassium-channel activation support repolarisation. Voltages, timing and conductances are illustrative and vary between cells. This neuronal waveform is not a universal muscle or pacemaker waveform.

figures.title: Conducting airways and gas-exchanging alveoli
figures.alt: Conducting airways are coloured red, alveoli blue; an inset shows surrounding capillaries and a conceptual oxygen and nitrogen washout graph.
figures.caption: The conducting zone carries gas; gas exchange begins in the respiratory zone. In the source’s washout key, horizontal position means exhaled volume and vertical position means relative gas concentration. The solid red oxygen-rich signal falls while the dashed blue nitrogen signal rises after breathing oxygen. The graph is qualitative, without calibrated axes; do not use it to calculate dead-space volume.

figures.title: Human pancreatic development: buds, position and growth
figures.alt: Composite fluorescence research figure locating the human developing pancreas, comparing separate and fused buds, and plotting dimensions across post-conceptional age. Panel descriptions and scale information follow the image.
figures.caption: Villalba et al. (2024), Figure 1. Human developmental specimens, not adult H&E. PCW denotes post-conceptional weeks; different specimens are compared, not followed as a time-lapse. SOX9 also labels non-pancreatic structures.
figures.rights: Villalba A, Gitton Y, Inoue M, et al. A 3D atlas of the human developing pancreas to explore progenitor proliferation and differentiation. Diabetologia 67:1066–1078 (2024). Figure 1. © The Author(s) 2024. CC BY 4.0
figures.publicApproval: Owner-authorised audited educational release; publisher CC BY 4.0 terms and figure-specific credits reviewed.
figures.modifications: Reproduced unchanged from the publisher PNG; no cropping, relabelling, recolouring or generated image content.
figures.observe: Compare panels c and d for separate and fused buds. Use scale bars before comparing dimensions, then distinguish an age-associated observation from a causal experiment.

panelDescriptions.label: Panels a and a′: whole-specimen orientation
panelDescriptions.text: Frontal and lateral views locate the pancreas in magenta in a PCW 7 specimen. SOX9 signal is also present in other organs and cartilage; it is not a pancreas-exclusive label. Scale bars: 2 mm.

panelDescriptions.label: Panel b: sagittal relationships
panelDescriptions.text: SOX9 and TH-labelled structures show the pancreatic region in relation to surrounding anatomy. Read the published channel labels, rather than treating fluorescence colours as H&E colours. Scale bar: 500 µm.

panelDescriptions.label: Panels c and d: compare buds
panelDescriptions.text: Panel c labels separate dorsal and ventral buds at PCW 5.7; panel d shows a fused configuration at PCW 6.4. These are different staged specimens. Scale bars: 200 µm.

panelDescriptions.label: Panel e: dissected pancreatic shapes
panelDescriptions.text: The series spans PCW 5–11 and shows changes in shape and size. Use the 500-µm scale bars; equal display height does not mean equal physical size.

panelDescriptions.label: Panels f–h: dimensions and their relationship
panelDescriptions.text: The plots report pancreatic length, diameter and the length-to-diameter relationship across sampled ages. They summarise a cross-sectional growth series, not repeated measurements of one embryo or a test of a causal signal.

figures.title: Mouse skeletal development: follow the labeling window
figures.alt: Mouse tibia fluorescence panels comparing embryonic timed labeling, a postnatal pulse and chase, and constitutive lineage labeling; two plots summarize labeled fractions. Adjacent text explains each panel group.
figures.caption: Long et al. (2022), Figure 1. Mouse fluorescence lineage tracing, not human H&E. A permanent label and current osteocalcin staining answer different questions. Scale bars: 100 µm. The source is 612 × 792 pixels; enlargement cannot create additional detail.
figures.rights: Long JT and colleagues. eLife 11:e76932 (2022), Figure 1. © 2022 Long et al. CC BY 4.0
figures.publicApproval: Owner-authorized educational release after source and rights audit; rendered release checks required.
figures.modifications: Unchanged publisher JPEG. No crop, relabeling, recoloring or generated content.
figures.observe: Read the genetic design and time window before interpreting the reporter. Compare a timed pulse with constitutive labeling without treating their denominators as identical.

panelDescriptions.label: Panels a–c: embryonic timed labeling
panelDescriptions.text: Induction at mouse embryonic days 13.5, 14.5 and 15.5 precedes the E16.5 observation. RFP reports the lineage label; OCN denotes osteocalcin staining. The two signals ask different questions about history and current phenotype.

panelDescriptions.label: Panels d–g: postnatal pulse and chase
panelDescriptions.text: Induction at P6 is followed by observations at 12 hours, 24 hours and two weeks. Panel g adds osteocalcin staining. Compare initial labeling with later location; these are sampled specimens, not a movie of one cell.

panelDescriptions.label: Panels h–k: constitutive labeling
panelDescriptions.text: These panels use constitutive Col10a1Cre labeling at two months, rather than the single P6 pulse. HZ denotes the hypertrophic zone and BM the marrow compartment. Location and osteocalcin signal help interpret labeled cells.

panelDescriptions.label: Panel l: two different denominators
panelDescriptions.text: The left plot considers reporter-positive cells among OCN-positive cells; the right considers labeled osteocytes among all counted osteocytes. Neither plot is the survival rate of a single pulse-labeled cohort. The article reports three biological replicates; plotted tissue sampling must not be mistaken for independent animals.

figures.title: Human choroid plexus: epithelial covering and vascular core

figures.caption: Tulemo, human lateral-ventricle choroid plexus, H&E, 50 µm scale bar. This permanently labelled photograph supports guided architectural interpretation. Age, disease state, fixation, embedding and section thickness are not supplied. Junctional strands, fenestrations and transporter molecules are not resolved here.
